This question (in a more generic form) has been legally debated for centuries. In itself, a work of fiction is mostly covered under free speech, but there are various state laws that restrict or prohibit interstate exchange of lewd, obscene or indecent material. Centuries ago, this applied both to travelers physically crossing state borders and to the content being mailed across states, and today, internet services are also often viewed in court as interstate exchange.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obscenity#Non_image-based_obscenity_cases_in_the_U.S.

  • Owning CP is illegal, and sharing it is illegal.
  • Owning "erotica" that depicts minors is arguably legal (free speech), but sharing it worldwide is still probably illegal.

This topic is very contentious, and things get way murkier when talking about drawings (lolicon). Is it illegal to draw minors engaged in sexual acts? Unlikely, as it falls under art. It is probably illegal to sell or distribute said art, though, as the various interstate obscenity laws will cover this.

On the same topic, would it be illegal to draw minors engaged in sexual acts, based on memories of an act that happened (i.e. non-fiction) ? For instance, a sexual abuse victim may want to draw a scene from their childhood, as a form of therapy. Rationally, it seems no different than reenactments, drawings or paintings of murder cases, or other material that can be judged as obscene as that.
